summary: Iteration 33 — verified the REVISED client-concern flow (single decision at modal level: 'Apply the changes' vs 'Keep as is & respond'; per-suggestion buttons deleted; unfreeze on concerns; lock flips share_status to 'sent'). 16/16 backend tests PASS on the new /review/apply-changes endpoint. Old /review/apply-suggestion endpoint correctly returns 405 (route removed). CRITICAL runtime bug found and fixed in ClientReviewModal.jsx: the leftover per-suggestion buttons block (lines ~287-314) still referenced undefined identifiers (`applyingIdx`, `applyChange`, `applySuggestion`), causing the WHOLE modal to crash with 'ReferenceError: applyingIdx is not defined' the moment any suggestion had `what_to_say` or `what_to_change` — which is EVERY realistic case. Removed the dead JSX block (spec explicitly said 'Per-suggestion buttons must NOT exist anymore'), and the entire flow now works end-to-end: modal opens → Apply the changes → backend maps ALL suggestions in parallel (~5-6s here) → toast '2 changes loaded — starting at Step 3' → navigate to /project/{id}/flow?step=3 → revision-banner lists both items each prefixed 'STEP 3'.

critical_code_review_comments: ClientReviewModal.jsx had leftover dead JSX from the previous per-suggestion design (`applyingIdx`, `applyChange`, `applySuggestion` all undefined) — this crashed the modal completely on every rejected/awaiting project that had suggestions with what_to_say/what_to_change. When you delete an old design path, delete BOTH the state (`applyingIdx`) AND the JSX consumers — leaving JSX behind is a runtime timebomb because JSX referencing undefined identifiers only fails at render, and only when that JSX branch is entered.

server.py step_lock still doesn't verify ownership — uses _get_project_or_404 (any authed user) not _get_owned_project_or_404. Inconsistent with unlock/reset-from-step. Not exploitable via UI today, but any leaked project id + an authed account elsewhere = privilege boundary broken.

apply_review_changes has a defensive `mapped = {step: 3, ...}` fallback if map_suggestion_to_step throws (line 1988) — good, but the fallback step is hardcoded to 3 regardless of the suggestion's `affects_step` hint. Could use `s.get('affects_step', 3)` for a smarter default.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 33 removed dead per-suggestion buttons from ClientReviewModal.jsx and rebuilt the backend test suite around /review/apply-changes. When testing similar dead-code cleanups, ALWAYS render the affected component with realistic seed data — a JSX branch that references an undefined identifier will only crash at render time, so a stub project without what_to_say/what_to_change would have silently passed. Also, the frontend uses PORTAL for the modal — pageerror listener catches the ReferenceError even though the DOM appears empty (modal never mounts).
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: The main agent removed the per-suggestion state (`applyingIdx`, `applyChange`, `applySuggestion`) at the top of ClientReviewModal.jsx as part of the flow rewrite, BUT left the JSX consumers (buttons at lines 287-314 inside the suggestions .map). JSX references identifiers by closure — since they no longer exist in scope, React threw `ReferenceError: applyingIdx is not defined` the moment Array.map hit any suggestion with `what_to_say || what_to_change` (which is EVERY real case). Because ClientReviewModal is portalled and the entire render throws, the modal never mounts — from the user's POV clicking 'View concerns & reply' does nothing. Reproduction: seed a rejected project with any suggestion having a `what_to_say` string, log in as owner, open the overview, click 'View concerns & reply' — Uncaught runtime errors overlay appears in dev, blank screen in prod. Fix: delete the dead JSX block. Verified working end-to-end: modal opens, both new decision actions present, Apply the changes navigates to flow?step=3 with a 2-item revision-banner.
